about: Space Hunter's cleanup items for macOS. Each item is one row in the app. See CONTRIBUTING.md for every field.

items.name: Temporary files
items.what: Your private temporary folder. Apps, installers and AI agents such as Claude Code or Codex write scratch files here while they work.
items.deletes: Files not changed within the age you set.
items.safe: Yes. On a Mac, open files can still be deleted, so keep the age at an hour or more.
items.after: Apps recreate what they need. macOS also clears this folder itself on restart.

items.name: App caches
items.short: Apps rebuild them; nothing you made
items.what: ~/Library/Caches: each app's disposable cache (browsers, Homebrew downloads, pip, Yarn and more).
items.deletes: Everything inside, except a few system caches that macOS protects.
items.safe: Yes. Caches are rebuildable by definition. Quit big apps first.
items.after: Apps feel slower once while rebuilding.

items.name: Logs & crash reports
items.what: ~/Library/Logs: app logs and crash reports.
items.deletes: All log files and crash reports.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: You can't send old crash reports to developers.

items.name: Browser code caches
items.short: Sites load slower once; logins kept
items.what: Compiled JavaScript and GPU caches kept by Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi and Arc (their normal caches sit in App caches).
items.deletes: Code Cache, GPUCache and Service Worker caches in each profile.
items.safe: Yes. Passwords, cookies, history, bookmarks and extensions are NOT touched.
items.after: Quit the browsers first for a full clean.

items.name: Chat app caches
items.what: Discord, Slack and Teams web caches.
items.deletes: Their cache folders.
items.safe: Yes. Messages and logins are kept.
items.after: Images re-download as you scroll.

items.name: Mail attachment copies
items.what: Every time you open an attachment in Apple Mail, Mail saves a copy here. The originals stay in your mailbox.
items.deletes: Those saved copies. Your emails and their attachments are not touched.
items.safe: Yes. macOS may ask for Full Disk Access to read this folder.
items.after: Opening an attachment again makes a fresh copy.

items.name: Adobe media cache
items.what: Premiere Pro, After Effects and Audition build preview and audio caches for every clip you import.
items.deletes: The Adobe media cache folders.
items.safe: Yes; Adobe rebuilds them. Close Adobe apps first.
items.after: Projects open a little slower the first time.

items.name: AI app caches & logs (e.g. Claude)
items.short: Apps open slower once; chats kept
items.what: AI desktop apps such as Claude keep a web cache, GPU and shader caches, and logs, like a browser does.
items.deletes: Those folders only. Not your chats, agent sessions or settings.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: Quit the app first for a full clean.

items.name: Code editor caches & logs
items.what: VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf keep a web cache, compiled-code cache and logs.
items.deletes: Cache, CachedData, Code Cache, GPUCache and logs.
items.safe: Yes. Extensions, settings and projects are untouched.
items.after: Rebuilt on the next start.

items.name: npm download cache
items.what: npm's download cache: a copy of every package you or an AI agent installed.
items.deletes: ~/.npm/_cacache. Same as 'npm cache clean --force'.
items.safe: Yes. Projects' node_modules folders are untouched.
items.after: The next install downloads again.

items.name: uv download cache
items.short: Python packages re-download on next install
items.what: uv's download and build cache (pip's lives in App caches).
items.deletes: ~/.cache/uv. Same as 'uv cache clean'.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: Future installs download again.

items.name: Xcode DerivedData
items.short: Next build of each project is a full build
items.what: Intermediate build files Xcode creates for every project you've built. Often 10+ GB.
items.deletes: Everything in DerivedData.
items.safe: Yes. Xcode's own advice for odd build errors is to delete it.
items.after: The next build of each project is slower.

items.name: Spotify & Steam caches
items.short: Streams again; offline songs may re-download
items.what: Spotify's streaming cache and Steam's web cache. Spotify's can grow to several GB and can hold songs saved for offline listening.
items.deletes: Those cache folders.
items.safe: Yes, if you don't mind re-downloading offline songs.
items.after: Songs saved for offline listening may need downloading again.

items.name: AI agent VM images (e.g. Claude Cowork)
items.what: Some AI desktop apps run agent tasks inside a Linux virtual machine (for example Claude's Cowork).
items.deletes: The virtual-machine image folders.
items.safe: Safe, but costly: the app downloads it again. Quit the app first.
items.after: The first agent task afterwards waits for the download.

items.name: Downloaded AI models
items.what: AI models and datasets downloaded by Python tools (Hugging Face, PyTorch). Some are many GB each.
items.deletes: Everything in those model caches.
items.safe: Only if you don't need them offline.
items.after: Scripts download them again.

items.name: AI tool runtimes (e.g. Codex)
items.what: Runtime environments that command-line AI tools such as Codex download for themselves.
items.deletes: ~/.cache/codex-runtimes.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The tool's next run is slower.

items.name: npx packages (MCP servers, tools)
items.what: Packages fetched by 'npx', including MCP servers that AI agents such as Claude or Codex start.
items.deletes: ~/.npm/_npx.
items.safe: Yes, if those tools aren't running. Quit your AI tools first.
items.after: Each tool downloads itself again on its next start.

items.name: Browser-automation browsers
items.what: Browser builds downloaded for browser-automation tools, which AI agents often use.
items.deletes: ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright.
items.safe: Yes, if no automation is running.
items.after: Tools download the browsers again when needed.

items.name: pnpm package store
items.what: pnpm keeps one shared copy of every package your projects use and links projects to it.
items.deletes: The whole store. Projects you already installed keep working, because their files are linked, not copied.
items.safe: Yes, but 'pnpm store prune' is gentler: it only removes packages no project uses.
items.after: The next pnpm install downloads packages again.

items.name: Gradle caches
items.short: Next build is slow and needs internet
items.what: Libraries Gradle downloaded for Android or Java projects.
items.deletes: ~/.gradle/caches.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build is slow and needs internet.

items.name: Maven packages
items.what: Maven's local repository: every Java library your builds downloaded.
items.deletes: Everything in ~/.m2/repository. Your settings file is kept.
items.safe: Yes, unless you installed your own libraries there with 'mvn install'.
items.after: The next build downloads libraries again and needs internet.

items.name: NuGet packages
items.what: Packages NuGet downloaded for .NET projects.
items.deletes: ~/.nuget/packages.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build restores packages.

items.name: Rust (Cargo) downloads
items.what: Cargo keeps every crate it downloaded, both packed and unpacked.
items.deletes: The registry cache, unpacked sources and git checkouts. Installed tools in ~/.cargo/bin are kept.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build downloads crates again and needs internet.

items.name: Go module downloads
items.what: Every Go module your builds downloaded.
items.deletes: Everything in ~/go/pkg/mod. Same as 'go clean -modcache'.
items.safe: Yes.
items.after: The next build downloads modules again and needs internet.

items.name: conda package cache
items.what: conda keeps every package it downloaded, packed and unpacked, in a pkgs folder.
items.deletes: Everything in the pkgs folders.
items.safe: Usually, but 'conda clean --all' is the gentler way: environments that link to these packages can break.
items.after: Creating a new environment downloads packages again.

items.name: Game engine caches (e.g. Unity, Unreal)
items.short: Projects open slower once while it rebuilds
items.what: Unity keeps downloaded packages and Asset Store downloads; Unreal keeps a shared cache of compiled shaders and assets (DerivedDataCache), often many GB.
items.deletes: Those cache folders. Your projects are untouched.
items.safe: Yes. Close the editors first.
items.after: Projects take longer to open once while the caches rebuild; Asset Store packages download again.

items.name: Android emulator snapshots & caches
items.what: The Android emulator saves a snapshot of each virtual phone so it starts fast. Each can be several GB.
items.deletes: The snapshots and the emulator cache. The virtual phones themselves and their apps are kept.
items.safe: Yes. Close the emulator first.
items.after: Each virtual phone does a full boot the next time, which is slower.

items.name: Xcode device support & simulator caches
items.short: Re-copied next time you debug a device
items.what: Symbols Xcode copies from every iOS version you've debugged on, plus simulator caches. Often several GB per version.
items.deletes: iOS DeviceSupport and CoreSimulator caches.
items.safe: Yes. Simulators themselves are untouched.
items.after: Plugging in a device re-copies its symbols.

items.name: Trash
items.what: Files you moved to the Trash.
items.deletes: Everything in your Trash. macOS may ask for Full Disk Access to read it.
items.safe: Only if you're sure; this is permanent.
items.after: Nothing can be restored.

items.name: Old AI agent chat history (Claude Code, Codex)
items.short: Those chats can't be resumed; memory kept
items.what: AI coding agents such as Claude Code (~/.claude) and Codex (~/.codex) save every conversation, sub-tasks and big tool outputs, plus checkpoints for undo.
items.deletes: Conversation and checkpoint files not changed within the age you set. Agents' memory folders (such as Claude's memory) are always skipped.
items.safe: Only for conversations you'll never reopen. Recent ones are protected by the age rule.
items.after: Those conversations can't be resumed or rewound.

items.name: Old AI agent workspaces (e.g. Claude 'No folder')
items.short: Their files are gone for good
items.what: When an AI agent session starts without a chosen folder (for example a Claude 'No folder' session), the app makes a private folder for it.
items.deletes: Whole session folders where nothing changed within the age you set.
items.safe: CAREFUL: these can hold real work. Check the folders below, or keep the ones you want.
items.after: That session's files are gone. Move anything you want into a real folder first.

items.name: Old iPhone & iPad backups
items.what: Every time a Mac backs up an iPhone or iPad, it keeps a full copy of the device here. Each backup can be 10-100 GB, and backups of old devices are never removed.
items.deletes: Whole backups that haven't changed within the age you set (90 days by default). Newer backups are kept.
items.safe: Only if those devices are backed up to iCloud, or you no longer need them. Check under Finder > your device > Manage Backups.
items.after: Those backups are gone, so you can't restore a device from them.

items.name: Old installers & archives in Downloads
items.short: Installers and archives only, top level
items.what: Disk images, installers and archives that pile up in Downloads after you've installed or unpacked them.
items.deletes: Only .dmg, .pkg, .zip, .7z, .rar, .iso and similar files sitting directly in Downloads, untouched for the age you set (30 days by default). Sub-folders and every other file type are never touched.
items.safe: Usually. Check the folder first if you keep installers you can't download again.
items.after: You'd need to download those installers again.
